name: SQL Injection Testing
description: Identification and exploitation of SQL injection vulnerabilities across all variants (in-band, blind, out-of-band). Covers detection via manual testing and automated tools, database-specific exploitation techniques, WAF bypass, and second-order injection.

0.label: None
0.description: No exposure to SQL injection testing

1.label: Awareness
1.description: Understands SQL injection concepts and basic attack vectors
evidence: Can explain the difference between in-band, blind, and out-of-band SQLi
Completed introductory training (e.g., OWASP WebGoat SQLi modules)
Can describe parameterised queries and why they prevent SQLi

2.label: Guided Practice
2.description: Detects and exploits basic SQLi under supervision using standard tooling
evidence: Identified SQLi in lab environments using manual techniques and sqlmap
Performed supervised SQLi testing on at least 2 engagements
Work reviewed and findings confirmed by authorized tester

3.label: Independent Practice
3.description: Independently identifies and exploits SQLi across common database platforms
evidence: Demonstrated SQLi exploitation across MySQL, PostgreSQL, and MSSQL
Independently identified SQLi on 5+ engagements with accurate risk ratings
Can perform blind SQLi extraction and document impact clearly
Passed proficiency assessment covering multiple SQLi variants

4.label: Advanced / Mentor
4.description: Exploits complex SQLi scenarios; bypasses WAFs; mentors junior testers
evidence: Demonstrated WAF bypass techniques for SQLi payloads
Identified second-order and stored procedure injection vulnerabilities
Develops custom tamper scripts for sqlmap or equivalent tooling
Reviews and mentors junior testers on SQLi findings

5.label: Expert / Authority
5.description: Recognized authority on SQLi; discovers novel techniques; trains teams
evidence: Published research or CVEs related to SQL injection
Developed lab methodology and training materials for SQLi testing
Handles novel database platforms and edge-case injection vectors
Trains teams on advanced SQLi techniques

assessment_methods.description: Detect and exploit SQLi in a prepared lab application with multiple injection points across different database backends
Review of SQLi findings from 3 recent engagement reports for accuracy and completeness
